cards.title: Fe 26.3 is here
headline: Fe 26.3
is here.
cards.description:
More expressive contracts.
Better tools to build them.
cards.alt: Fe 26.3 is here. A violet gradient release card with the Fe logo and the themes Memory, Interoperability, and Debugging foundations.
cards.tweet:
Fe 26.3 is here!

First-class memory pointers, new array and ERC-20 helpers, important compiler fixes, and foundations for source-level debugging.

Here's what's new ->

cards.title: Memory gets a type.
cards.subtitle: First-class pointers: *T
cards.code:
use core::ptr

let p: *u256 = ptr::alloc<u256>()
*p = 41
*p += 1
assert!(*p == 42)
cards.note: Pointers also support field access and mutable array indexing.
cards.alt: Fe code allocates a u256 pointer, writes 41, increments it, and checks that it reads 42. Side labels explain allocation, dereference, and prevention of storage escape.
cards.tweet:
Fe now has first-class memory pointers: *T.

Allocate typed memory, read and write through dereferences, access fields, and index pointer-backed arrays.

The compiler also prevents pointer-bearing values from escaping into persistent or transient storage.

cards.title: Views, length, capacity.
cards.subtitle: Explicit memory regions for ABI and EVM operations.
cards.note: MemSlice<T>: typed views. FixedMemBuffer<N>: fixed-size owned allocation.
cards.alt: A MemBuffer allocation has ten blocks, with six marked as bytes in use. Length spans the used bytes; capacity spans the full allocation. MemSpan provides a read-only byte view. The previous low-level memory API is replaced.
cards.tweet:
Memory APIs now distinguish read-only views from owned allocations:

- MemSlice<T> / MemSpan: read-only views
- MemBuffer: owned memory with length and capacity
- FixedMemBuffer<N>: fixed-size allocation

This replaces the previous low-level memory API.

cards.title: Separate maps. Separate salts.
cards.subtitle: Independent inferred layout values for nested storage maps.
cards.caption: Repeated types no longer accidentally share inferred salts.
cards.note: Contract and field hovers now expose the assigned layout.
cards.alt: Two independent lanes connect store.balances to inferred salt A and store.allowances to inferred salt B. Distinct nested maps no longer accidentally share inferred salts; editor hovers expose the layout.
cards.tweet:
An important correctness fix: nested storage maps now receive independent inferred layout values.

Previously, distinct maps could accidentally share a salt and overwrite each other's data.

Editor hovers now also show layouts grouped by storage, transient storage, and code.

cards.title: Build an ABI array in memory.
cards.subtitle: MemVec<T> + DynArray<T>
cards.note: Length stays fixed. DynArray<T>.get(index) provides typed element reads.
cards.alt: Fe code creates a three-element MemVec of u256, writes 100, 200, and 300, then creates an independent DynArray snapshot. Length is fixed at creation; DynArray.get reads typed elements.
cards.tweet:
Working with ABI arrays is easier:

- DynArray<T>.get(index) reads typed elements
- MemVec<T> provides mutable memory arrays
- .to_dyn_array() creates an independent ABI-encodable snapshot

MemVec's length is set at creation; it does not grow.

cards.title: Compare the whole collection.
cards.subtitle: == and != for fixed-size arrays and tuples.
cards.code:
let a: [u256; 3] = [1, 2, 3]
assert!(a == [1, 2, 3])

let pair: (u256, bool) = (7, true)
assert!(pair != (7, false))
cards.note: Tuples support zero through six elements; array elements must implement Eq.
cards.alt: Code compares a u256 array with an equal array and compares the tuple (7, true) with (7, false). Equality uses element Eq implementations, short-circuits, and supports nesting without requiring Copy. Tuples support up to six elements.
cards.tweet:
Arrays and tuples now support == and != when their elements implement Eq.

Comparisons work recursively, respect custom equality, and stop at the first mismatch.

Fixed-size arrays and tuples of up to six elements are supported, including the empty tuple.

cards.title: Dynamic arrays in events.
cards.subtitle: Fixed Solidity signatures for non-indexed dynamic array fields.
cards.note: Indexed dynamic fields remain unsupported and receive a targeted diagnostic.
cards.alt: An event struct ValuesChanged with a DynArray<u256> field resolves to ValuesChanged(uint256[]). TOPIC0 is the keccak256 hash of that signature. Indexed dynamic fields remain unsupported.
cards.tweet:
Dynamic array event fields now produce correct Solidity signatures.

A ValuesChanged event containing DynArray<u256> gets the signature:

ValuesChanged(uint256[])

Aliases and nested array types work too. Indexed dynamic fields remain unsupported.

cards.title: Packed bytes. Direct hashes.
cards.subtitle: No word padding. No length prefixes.
cards.note: Also new: a growable Packed builder and crypto::eip712_digest.
cards.alt: Packed encoding concatenates a u16 as two bytes, an Address as twenty bytes, and a bool as one byte. Labelled blocks are schematic, not to scale. keccak_packed hashes the same bytes directly, without ABI word padding or length prefixes.
cards.tweet:
New packed encoding helpers:

- encode_packed builds byte payloads
- keccak_packed hashes them directly
- Packed builds payloads incrementally

There's also eip712_digest(domain_separator: ..., struct_hash: ...) for the final EIP-712 digest.

cards.title: One API. Both token conventions.
cards.subtitle: safe_transfer / safe_transfer_from / safe_approve
cards.note: Token reverts propagate. safe_approve does not automatically reset allowances.
cards.alt: ERC-20 helper outcomes: true is accepted; empty return data from an address with contract code is accepted; false and targets without code revert. Token revert data propagates. safe_approve does not reset allowances automatically.
cards.tweet:
ERC-20 tokens don't all return data the same way.

New safe_transfer, safe_transfer_from, and safe_approve helpers accept true or empty returndata, reject false and targets without code, and propagate token reverts.

cards.title: Messages become calls.
cards.subtitle: Typed STATICCALLs and calldata helpers.
cards.caption: Address::static  /  encode_msg_calldata  /  call_with_default
cards.note: call_with_default uses the default only for successful calls with empty returndata.
cards.alt: A four-step diagram shows a Fe message encoded as calldata, sent to a contract with CALL or STATICCALL, then decoded from returndata. Address.static, encode_msg_calldata, and call_with_default support the workflow.
cards.tweet:
More tools for external calls:

- Address::static makes typed STATICCALLs
- encode_msg_calldata prepares selector + arguments
- call_with_default handles successful calls with empty returndata

Non-empty returndata is still decoded strictly.

cards.title: Rebuild from one JSON file.
cards.subtitle: fe build --from-metadata out/Token.metadata.json
cards.caption: A building block for verification and external toolchains.
cards.note: Matching original bytecode requires the original compiler and settings.
cards.alt: Metadata containing sources and settings goes through the Fe compiler to produce bytecode. Command: fe build --from-metadata out/Token.metadata.json. Exact reproduction requires matching the original compiler and settings.
cards.tweet:
Fe 26.2 added contract metadata. Fe 26.3 adds rebuilding from it:

fe build --from-metadata out/Token.metadata.json

The compiler reconstructs the project and uses its recorded settings - a building block for source verification and external tooling.

cards.title: Debugging starts here.
cards.subtitle: Experimental foundations for bytecode-to-source attribution.
cards.caption: Developer trace commands + a Fe-specific ethdebug export.
cards.note: Partial coverage. Unstable APIs. Stock ethdebug compatibility is not established.
cards.alt: A conceptual attribution pipeline links Fe source, MIR compiler facts, the Sonatina backend, and emitted EVM instructions at program-counter offsets. The Fe-specific ethdebug export is experimental: coverage is partial, APIs are unstable, and compatibility with stock ethdebug consumers is not established.
cards.tweet:
Source-level debugging foundations are landing.

New developer commands track bytecode-to-source attribution and export an experimental Fe-specific ethdebug view.

Coverage is partial, APIs are unstable, and compatibility with existing ethdebug tools is not yet established.

cards.title: A smoother compile cycle.
cards.subtitle: Fewer surprises when contracts get more complex.

items.label: TYPE INFERENCE
items.text:
Better trait resolution
and match diagnostics

items.label: WIDE CALLS
items.text:
More than 16 arguments
in functions and recv arms

items.label: DIAGNOSTICS
items.text:
Useful errors in cases
that previously crashed

cards.alt: Four compiler improvements: better trait inference and match diagnostics; functions and recv arms with more than sixteen arguments; function deduplication after monomorphization; and useful diagnostics instead of compiler crashes.
cards.tweet:
Compiler improvements include:

- Better trait inference and match diagnostics
- Support for functions and recv arms with >16 arguments
- Function deduplication to reduce compile time
- More useful errors where the compiler previously crashed

There's more: integer square roots, new StorageBytes reads, wrapping arithmetic for Solidity integer types, and missing usize assignment operators.

Read the full announcement, including migration notes for the memory APIs:
